### [1] Triedman, Jha, Shmatikov. "Attacking Multi-Agent Systems via Control-Flow Hijacking." COLM 2025.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12188
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** Attack success rates by orchestrator/model: Magentic-One/GPT-4o 58-97%, Selector/GPT-4o-mini 98%, Round-Robin/GPT-4o-mini 100%, CrewAI/GPT-4o 62-68%, MetaGPT/GPT-4o 90%. Attacks succeed even when individual agents refuse harmful actions. Exfiltration: CrewAI GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini 65%.

### [2] Chen et al. "Agent-in-the-Middle Attack on Multi-Agent Systems." 2025.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14847
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** AiTM attack exploits inter-agent communication mechanisms. LLM-powered adversarial agent with reflection mechanism generates contextually-aware malicious instructions. Framework-agnostic across AutoGen and Camel.

### [3] ToolHijacker. "Tool Selection Manipulation in LLM Agents." NDSS 2026.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19793
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** Injects malicious tool documents into tool libraries using two-phase optimization. Outperforms existing prompt injection attacks on tool selection. Defenses (StruQ, SecAlign, KAD, DataSentinel, perplexity detection) insufficient.

### [4] SEAgent. "Mandatory Access Control Framework for LLM Agent Systems." 2026.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.11893
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** ABAC framework with 5 tool attributes (Object, Action, Sensitivity, Privacy, Integrity). 0% ASR across all benchmarked attacks (InjecAgent, AgentDojo). False positive rate: 0% (1-2 tools), 5.13% (≥3 tools). Execution time on par with naive agent. IsolateGPT comparison: 2-4× slower with 18% FPR. Multi-agent evaluation: goal success +10.7%, tokens −38%.

### [5] PFI. "Prompt Flow Integrity for LLM Agents." 2025.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15547
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** Three mitigation techniques: agent isolation, secure untrusted data processing, privilege escalation guardrails. Privileged (TP) and unprivileged (TU) access tokens. Effectively mitigates privilege escalation while preserving utility.

### [6] MiniScope. "Least Privilege Framework for Tool-Calling Agents." 2025.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11147
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** Automatically constructs permission hierarchies. Mobile-style permission model. 1-6% latency overhead vs vanilla tool-calling agents. Outperforms LLM-based baselines on permission minimization, computational cost, and operational cost.

### [7] Progent. "Privilege Control Mechanism for LLM Agents." 2025.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11703
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** First privilege control framework with DSL for fine-grained tool policies. 0% ASR on AgentDojo, ASB, AgentPoison benchmarks. Preserves agent utility and speed. LLMs can automatically generate effective policies. Modular with minimal implementation changes.

### [8] AgentDojo. "Benchmark for Prompt Injection Defenses in AI Agents." NeurIPS 2024.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13352
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** 97 tasks, 629 security test cases. GPT-4o baseline: 69% benign utility, 57.69% targeted ASR. Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 78.22% utility, 33.86% ASR. Tool filter defense: 6.84% ASR (from 57.69%). Prompt injection detector: 7.95% ASR but utility drops to 41.49%. Slack suite: 92% ASR.

### [9] MINJA. "Memory Injection Attacks Against LLM Agents." 2026.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05504
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** Query-only attack achieving >95% ISR and 70% ASR under idealized conditions. Tested on GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-2.0-Flash, Llama-3.1-8B. Effectiveness drops with pre-existing legitimate memories. Defenses: composite trust scoring, trust-aware retrieval with temporal decay.

### [10] AgentPoison. "Backdoor Attack on RAG-Based LLM Agents." NeurIPS 2024.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12784
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** ≥80% ASR with <0.1% poison rate and <1% benign performance degradation. No model training needed. Tested on RAG-based autonomous driving, QA, and healthcare agents. Superior transferability and stealthiness.

### [11] ARCJ. "Contagious Jailbreak in Multi-Agent Systems." 2024.

- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** Adversarial Replication Contagious Jailbreak with retrieval and replication suffix optimization. Improvements: line topology 23.51%, star topology 18.95%, 100-agent settings 52.93%. "Toxicity disappearing" phenomenon in non-complete graphs.

### [19] Google DeepMind. "Lessons from Defending Gemini Against Indirect Prompt Injections." 2025.
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/html/2505.14534v1
- **Tier:** 1
- **Data extracted:** Five lessons: capability ≠ security, adaptive evaluation critical, adversarial training works without degradation, defense-in-depth required, focus on real-world harm. TAP attack: ~100% ASR against undefended Gemini 2.0 at <$10 cost. Static benchmarks create false confidence.
